ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, $\triangle PAC \cong \triangle PBD$, given that $\angle A=40^\circ$ and $\angle BPD=20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle PCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $\triangle PAC \cong \triangle PBD$,\\
it follows that $\angle A=\angle B, \angle APC=\angle BPD, \angle PCA=\angle PDB$\\
Since $\angle A=40^\circ, \angle BPD=20^\circ$\\
it follows that $\angle APC=20^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle PCD=\angle A+\angle APC=40^\circ+20^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: P is the top vertex, A,C,D,B lie on one straight horizontal line in that order, and segments PA, PC, PD, PB are drawn. From the text, use the congruence statement triangle PAC congruent to triangle PBD with vertex order P-A-C corresponding to P-B-D. Therefore angle APC corresponds to angle BPD, so angle APC = 20 degrees, and angle PAC = angle A = 40 degrees. Since CD is the extension of CA through C in the image, angle PCD is the exterior angle at C of triangle PAC. Apply the exterior angle theorem: angle PCD = angle PAC + angle APC = 40 + 20 = 60 degrees.
